_comment: Guided tour for FRET-2CDE / ALEX-2CDE. The panel is hand-built Qt, not an AutoForm view, so steps target objectNames -- the shared action buttons by suffix ({'name': 'run'} finds toolAction_run) and the settings fields by the twocde_* names set in gui/tool.py. Read by chisurf.gui.widgets.tools.guided_tour.

steps.title: Did it stay there, or did it move?
steps.text:
A burst's mean FRET efficiency says where the molecule sat. It does not say whether it stayed there — a molecule that switches state while crossing the focus lands at some intermediate E, and on the histogram that is indistinguishable from a genuinely static intermediate.

2CDE separates the two from the photon arrival times alone: one number per burst, no kinetic model, no binning.

Seven steps.

steps.title: The burst folder, not the raw files
steps.text:
2CDE reads a finished burst-analysis folder — the bursts are already defined, and this adds a column to them. It re-opens the raw measurements named in that folder's manifest to get the photon times, so both have to be reachable.

You can also drop the folder onto this window.

await.hint: Press the folder button and choose the burst-analysis folder.

steps.title: Two different questions, one machinery
steps.text:
FRET-2CDE asks whether donor and acceptor brightness rise and fall together. In a static burst they do — both track the same molecule crossing the beam — and the score sits near a baseline of ≈ 10 whatever the efficiency is. Switch state mid-burst and the two colours anticorrelate in time; the score climbs into 30–100 for clear millisecond dynamics.

ALEX-2CDE runs the same estimator on the two excitation streams and scores brightness heterogeneity: donor-only and acceptor-only species, an acceptor that blinks mid-burst, two molecules coinciding. It needs ALEX or PIE data.

One run computes one of them, not both. With ALEX data, screen with ALEX-2CDE first — several of the things that raise FRET-2CDE are impurities, not conformation.

steps.title: τ is the window, and it is the only window
steps.text:
τ sets the timescale over which brightness is averaged — short enough to resolve a change within a burst, long enough to collect several photons per kernel. 40–100 µs sits between the microsecond photon spacing and the millisecond transit.

It is also the limit of what you can see. Exchange much faster than τ is averaged away inside the kernel; exchange much slower than the ~1 ms transit never happens while you are watching. Both look static.

So a baseline score means "no dynamics in this window", never "no dynamics". Change τ and run again before concluding anything.

steps.title: Laplace or Gaussian, and why you might switch
steps.text:
Laplace is Tomov's original and what a comparison against the literature must use.

Gaussian estimates the local rate more accurately and depends far less on where it is evaluated — the Laplace kernel, sampled at the photon positions, always sits on its own peak and over-estimates the rate.

Below the fields: the donor and acceptor routing channels. Get them backwards and the analysis still completes and still looks plausible.

steps.title: Run it
steps.text:
The kernel density runs over the whole photon stream and is sliced per burst afterwards — deliberately, because restricting it to the burst would put an artificial cliff at each boundary and inflate the score for short bursts.

It takes minutes on a real folder, off the GUI thread, and ⏹ stops it. The result is written to a 2c4/ companion beside the burst tables, one row per burst, so the browser and ndX can gate on the column.

steps.title: Read it against the baseline, not against zero
steps.text:
The plot is 2CDE against the burst's proximity ratio. The static population is the horizontal band near 10; dynamic bursts sit above it.

Three things before you believe a dynamic fraction:
1. The baseline is a statistic, not a constant. Dim bursts scatter around it far more widely, so a fixed cutoff flags proportionally more of them purely by shot noise. Cut on photon count first.
2. NaN rows are not zeros. A burst with an empty donor or acceptor stream has no ratio at all; the status line says how many of the bursts were valid.
3. It is a flag, not a rate. 2CDE says a burst changed — not how fast, how many states, or which way. Select on it, then fit the selection with H2MM or PDA.

The ? button has the rest.
